answer: A defense pairs a per-identity throughput cap with a fixed emission ceiling. Each agent submits one scored entry per epoch at most, and the Nebula layer mints a constant pool however many identities exist, so extra identities only split it thinner. A Raven watcher sampled from established peers flags clusters sharing timing and fingerprints. The attacker's math: N identities cost N deposits plus upkeep while income stays capped, so once per-identity reward falls below the 0.4-token maintenance cost, each sybil is pure loss and a real agent's signal is uneconomical to fake.
